newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Democrats return $1.5 in campaign funds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Democrats return $1.5 in campaign funds.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's Democratic party announced on Friday it was returning $1.5 million in 1996 campaign donations that may have been illegal or inappropriate under U.S. campaign finance laws.

The party's new national chairman, Gov. Roy Romer of Colorado, said at a news conference that as a result of an audit of Democratic fundraising, "We will return contributions from 77 donors totalling $1.5 million."

"That's a serious amount but it's a small percentage of the overall amount raised," Romer said. "...But to admit the mistake and to take corrective action is not enough. We need to make changes so that it won't happen again, and we have done so." He said the reforms would "apply a new discipline" to Democratic fund-raising.

The announcement was the latest in a series of revelations on Democratic Party fund-raising that have dogged Clinton and his party since he was re-elected last November. On Tuesday the White House released internal memos showing that Clinton took a leading role in efforts to woo major party financial supporters by inviting them to special White House events.

Romer did not specify why the $1.5 million in campaign donations was being returned, or to whom. But he said the audit had established that careless fund-raising practices had led the party to accept some funds that were illegal, inappropriate or at least questionable.

The sum being returned more than doubled the amount the Democrats had already announced they were sending back to donors. They had already returned about $1.47 million, much of it linked to sources in Asia, including some with interests in U.S. foreign or trade policy. Only Americans or foreigners living legally in the United States can donate to federal election campaigns.
